artists.biography: Charles Bradley (born 1948, Gainesville, Florida), commonly referred to as "The Screaming Eagle of Soul," is a funk/soul/R&B singer signed to the Daptone Records label under the Dunham Records division. His performances and recording style are consistent with Daptone's revivalist approach, celebrating the feel of funk and soul music from the 1960s and 1970s. One review stated that Bradley "echoes the evocative delivery of Otis Redding". He is the subject of a documentary, Soul of America, that premiered at SXSW in 2012.
artists.name: Charles Bradley

artists.biography:
The Menahan Street Band is a Brooklyn, New York-based instrumental band formed in 2007, that plays funk and soul music. The band features musicians from Antibalas, El Michels Affair, Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings and the Budos Band. The group was founded by Thomas Brenneck while living in an apartment on Menahan St. in the Brooklyn neighborhood of Bushwick. Their debut album, Make the Road by Walking, was released in 2008 on Dunham, a sublabel of Daptone Records.

After Jay Z sampled the album's title track for his hit single "Roc Boys (And the Winner Is…)", the band invested their royalty money from the song in building a studio. Brenneck launched the all-analog Dunham Sound Studios, and the band worked there for many months on the completion of their 2012 sophomore album The Crossing.

perplexity.description:
Black Velvet is the fourth and final studio album by American funk and soul artist Charles Bradley, released posthumously on November 9, 2018, by Dunham Records. The album compiles previously unreleased tracks recorded during sessions for Bradley’s earlier albums—No Time for Dreaming (2011), Victim of Love (2013), and Changes (2016)—and was assembled by producer Thomas Brenneck after Bradley’s death from cancer in September 2017. Musically, the album stays true to Bradley’s signature revivalist style, blending raw, emotive soul vocals with classic funk instrumentation provided by the Menahan Street Band. The tracklist includes original songs, a duet with LaRose Jackson (“Luv Jones”), alternate takes, and covers of “Stay Away” by Nirvana, “Heart of Gold” by Neil Young, and “Slip Away” by Rodriguez, showcasing Bradley’s ability to reinterpret diverse material with deep feeling.

As the last release in Bradley’s discography, Black Velvet serves as a fitting tribute to his legacy as the “Screaming Eagle of Soul.” The album’s title references Bradley’s stage name during his years as a James Brown impersonator, reflecting his roots and enduring connection to classic soul performance. While not as commercially dominant as his earlier works, Black Velvet reached number 7 on the US Independent Albums chart and charted in several European countries. Critics praised the album for its emotional depth and authenticity, highlighting its role in preserving Bradley’s powerful voice and artistry for new generations of soul and funk listeners.
